title: The recursive-construction conjecture for permanents of 312-avoiding matrices
statement:
Let $f_{312}(n)$ be the maximum permanent of an $n\times n$ 0-1 matrix avoiding the permutation pattern 312. Let $\mathcal{M}_n(\ast,\circ)$ be the set of $n\times n$ matrices obtained by starting with $1\times1$ identity matrices and repeatedly applying the two operations $\ast$ and $\circ$ in any order. **Recursive-construction conjecture.** For every $n\geq1$,

$$
f_{312}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{per}(A):A\in\mathcal{M}_n(\ast,\circ)\}.
$$

The conjecture concerns whether the displayed recursive operations always contain an extremal construction. The source states it as open and does not provide a proof or counterexample.
source_name: Adam Zsolt Wagner, “Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks”, arXiv:2104.14516 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14516

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2021). “The conjecture regarding the location of the peak was disproved by Collins who showed that for paths the peak is at index approximately $\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)n$.”
